rows.grounds: ritual act of claiming the site

items.question: What initial actions must be performed to prepare the ritual ground?
premises: The ground must first be taken into possession.
Its measurement must be determined on all sides.
items.inference: Ritual preparation begins with claiming and measuring the ground completely.
items.plain_english: Having taken possession of the ground and measured it on all sides,

items.question: What measurements are prescribed for the ritual site in a village and a city?
premises: In a village the site is measured as one krośa.
In a city the prescribed measure is twice that.
items.inference: The required extent of the ritual ground varies by settlement type.
items.plain_english: In a village the place is prescribed as one krośa in measure, and in a city twice that.

items.question: What protective ritual actions must be performed in the ten directions?
premises: The weapon should be buried in the ten directions.
The weapon should also be worshipped.
items.inference: Directional protection requires both installation and worship of the weapon.
items.plain_english: One should bury the weapon in the ten directions and worship it.

items.question: Who should worship the field guardians and related deities at the site?
premises: The field guardians and others are to be worshipped there.
The worship should be performed by one most skilled in ritual.
items.inference: A qualified ritual expert must honor the site guardians.
items.plain_english: There the one most skilled in ritual should worship the field guardians and others.

items.question: What condition invalidates the performance of a recitation sacrifice?
premises: The tortoise-wheel must be known for the rite.
Someone may perform the recitation sacrifice without knowing it.
items.inference: Performing the recitation sacrifice without knowledge of the tortoise-wheel is faulty.
items.plain_english: Whoever would perform a recitation sacrifice without knowing the tortoise-wheel,

items.question: What outcomes follow from knowing or not knowing the tortoise-wheel in recitation?
premises: With proper knowledge one obtains all the stated results.
Otherwise one meets with destruction.
items.inference: Knowledge of the tortoise-wheel determines success or ruin in the rite.
items.plain_english: obtains all the stated results; otherwise he goes to destruction.

items.question: How is the tortoise-wheel said to be arranged in the world?
premises: The tortoise-wheel is situated fourfold in the world.
Its manner is now explained.
items.inference: The tortoise-wheel has a fourfold arrangement that is to be described.
items.plain_english: It is situated fourfold in the world; its manner is stated thus.

items.question: What are the named forms in the fourfold arrangement of the tortoise-wheel?
premises: It is described as village-going and house-going.
It is arranged in four forms altogether.
items.inference: The tortoise-wheel is classified into four forms including village-going and house-going.
uncertainties: Only two of the four forms are explicitly named in this verse.
items.plain_english: As village-going and house-going, it is arranged fourfold.

items.question: How should the consonant groups be placed across the directional span?
premises: The span runs from east to west.
The groups from ka to ma should be placed along it.
items.inference: The consonant series from ka to ma is to be arranged from east to west.
items.plain_english: One should place the letters from ka to ma from the east to the west.

items.question: Where should the pair and the vowels be placed within the diagram?
premises: A pair is placed in the northeast.
The vowels are placed in the middle beginning from the east.
items.inference: The diagram requires specific placement of a pair in the northeast and vowels in the center.
uncertainties: The identity of the pair is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: One should place a pair in the northeast, and then place the vowels in the middle beginning from the east.

items.question: What bodily parts of the tortoise diagram are identified for placement?
premises: The diagram includes a face, sides, hands, belly, and feet.
These parts are assigned in their respective places.
items.inference: The tortoise-wheel is mapped onto distinct bodily parts of the tortoise.
items.plain_english: Its face, hands at the sides, belly, and feet are in their respective places.

items.question: What results arise from placement in the face and hands of the tortoise?
premises: Placement in the face yields success in all purposes.
Placement in the hands yields all successes.
items.inference: Different parts of the tortoise diagram confer different auspicious results.
items.plain_english: In the face there would be success in all purposes; in the hands, all successes.

items.question: What contrasting results are associated with the tail and other parts of the tortoise?
premises: Placement in the tail certainly brings death.
Other placements bring success in all purposes.
items.inference: The tail is an inauspicious location unlike the other parts.
uncertainties: The verse states both death and all-purpose successes; the latter may refer to remaining parts not named here.
items.plain_english: In the tail there is certainly death, but in the others there are successes in all purposes.

items.question: How should a wise practitioner prepare and recite the chosen mantra?
premises: The syllable should be made joined with bindu.
The wise one should then recite the chosen mantra.
items.inference: Proper mantra recitation requires adding bindu to the syllable.
items.plain_english: Having made the syllable joined with bindu, the wise one should recite his chosen mantra.

items.question: What syllable should be constructed as Meru in the ritual arrangement?
premises: The kṣa syllable is to be used.
It should be constructed there as Meru.
items.inference: The kṣa syllable functions as the Meru in this arrangement.
items.plain_english: Then, O Lady of the world, one should construct the kṣa syllable there as Meru.

items.question: What efficacy does this method confer on the recitation of all mantras?
premises: Recitation is performed by this method.
It applies to all mantras.
items.inference: By this method, recitation of any mantra accomplishes all purposes.
items.plain_english: By this method, the recitation of all mantras accomplishes all purposes.

items.question: What pattern of mantra recitation is prescribed to yield results?
premises: The mantra should be recited in an alternating one-by-one pattern.
Such recitation gives fruit.
items.inference: Alternating recitation of the mantra is an effective, fruit-giving method.
uncertainties: The exact alternation pattern is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: One should thus recite the mantra alternating one by one, as it gives fruit.

items.question: What is the source of the obstacles indicated by signs of facing that state?
premises: Signs of facing that state appear.
Obstacles arise from former causes and the like.
items.inference: Obstacles signaled in this context originate from prior causes.
uncertainties: The referent of 'that' and the exact signs are unclear from this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The signs of facing that are obstacles arising from former causes and so on.

items.question: What spiritual attainment can a mortal achieve through this practice?
premises: By this means even a mortal can succeed.
The attainment is liberation while living and becoming identified with the deity.
items.inference: The practice enables a mortal to attain living liberation and identity with the deity.
items.plain_english: By which even a mortal may succeed, becoming liberated while living and becoming one with me.

items.question: What preliminary acts are required before practicing the sequence in the red circle?
premises: The teacher must be satisfied with wealth.
After that one should practice the sequence in the red circle.
items.inference: Satisfying the guru precedes undertaking the ritual sequence in the red circle.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the red circle is not specified.
items.plain_english: Having satisfied the teacher with wealth, one should practice the sequence in the red circle.

items.question: What food offering should be presented in this ritual sequence?
premises: Milk rice-pudding is to be prepared.
It should include plantain, jaggery, and sugar.
items.inference: The prescribed offering is rice-pudding made with milk, plantain, jaggery, and sugar.
items.plain_english: One should offer rice-pudding made with milk, plantain, jaggery, and sugar.

items.question: What proportions and substances are prescribed for the fire offering and libation?
premises: The fire offering should be performed as a tenth part.
Libation should be performed with moon-water.
items.inference: The ritual requires a tenth-part fire offering and libation with moon-water.
uncertainties: The meaning of moon-water is not specified.
items.plain_english: One should perform the fire offering as a tenth part and the libation with moon-water.

items.question: What completion is achieved by performing the prescribed ritual procedure?
premises: The procedure should be performed as instructed.
By that the hundred-thousand becomes complete.
items.inference: Performing the procedure brings the hundred-thousand recitations to completion.
items.plain_english: One should perform it; by that, O Goddess, the hundred-thousand becomes fully complete.

items.question: How does the required recitation count change in the Tretā and Dvāpara ages?
premises: In the Tretā age the amount is twofold.
In the Dvāpara age it is prescribed as threefold.
items.inference: The required recitation count increases in later cosmic ages.
items.plain_english: In the Tretā age it is twofold, and likewise in the Dvāpara age it is prescribed as threefold.
